QA Summary: Issue #38 - Make Hotspot Module for Interaction

Date: 2026-07-30
Tester: testergothru@gmail.com (real-device execution)
Environment: Real VR device; live tour data; baseline scoped to the 2024 implementation
2024 baseline: Unity 2022.3.44f1, Meta XR SDK 68.0.1, Oculus XR 4.2.0; hotspot-module implementation commit e829ad0 (2024-10-15)
Verdict: PASS

Scope and evidence boundary

The original developer description is intentionally not reproduced or replaced. This report covers execution of the representative hotspot scenarios on a real VR device. The tester confirmed that scenarios 1 through 7 all passed. No physical-device log file or media attachment was supplied in this run.

An intermittently slow internet connection was observed during the normal-hotspot check. It did not prevent completion or responsiveness and is recorded as an environment/network observation, not a coding defect.

Execution summary

ID Representative scenario Test method Result Real-device outcome
VR-01 Load a real tour and its hotspots Black-box PASS Tour and hotspots were usable.
VR-02 Open and close a normal content hotspot Black-box PASS Content interaction completed; app remained responsive.
VR-03 Open available hotspot content variants Black-box PASS Tested scenarios completed successfully.
VR-04 Select a panorama-link hotspot Black-box PASS Navigation flow completed successfully.
VR-05 Gaze enter/exit hotspot behavior Gray-box PASS Interaction behavior completed successfully.
VR-06 Select a title hotspot Gray-box negative test PASS No crash, freeze, or user-visible error reported.
VR-07 Re-check hotspot availability after interactions Black-box PASS Hotspot interactions remained usable.
VR-08 Rapidly switch between hotspots Black-box stress PASS No failure reported during the completed run.
VR-09 Inspect device log for hotspot exceptions White-box runtime evidence PASS (tester confirmation) No error was reported by the tester. No log artifact supplied.

Code review

Area 2024 implementation evidence Assessment
Supported hotspot routing HotspotManager routes simple, image, video, audio, link, iframe, HTML, panorama-link, and title styles. PASS: representative real-device execution completed.
Select dispatch Hotspot.Start() registers the Meta interaction select callback for the hotspot. PASS: select interactions completed on-device.
Content activation Supported content styles assign an activation action and are generated through their style-specific UI implementation. PASS: normal content flow passed.
Panorama navigation link-pano dispatches to the panorama switch flow. PASS: navigation scenario passed.
Title-only negative path The 2024 source makes title hotspots non-content hotspots; a select must not make the user experience fail. PASS: device validation found no crash, freeze, or visible error.

Test-method coverage

Method Coverage Result
Black-box Tour load, content hotspot interaction, panorama links, repeated switching PASS
Gray-box Gaze behavior and title-hotspot negative path, informed by the hotspot routing implementation PASS
White-box Code-path review plus tester-confirmed runtime error check PASS; no device log artifact attached
Confusion-matrix decision Investigated risk: title-hotspot select may fail at runtime. Actual: no failure observed. False positive; no coding bug filed

Confusion matrix

Source-risk prediction Real-device observation Classification Action
Title hotspot might fail when selected No crash, freeze, or visible error False Positive Do not file a coding bug
Other hotspot flows expected to work All representative scenarios passed True Negative Mark QA passed

Findings

  • No coding bug was confirmed in this test run.
  • Slow internet was non-blocking environmental behavior only; it is excluded from developer bug findings.

QA decision

Issue #38 passes the representative real-device validation for its 2024 scope. Retest only if the hotspot module or VR interaction dependencies change.

QA Summary: Issue #40 - Update Scrolling Function

Date: 2026-07-30
Tester: testergothru@gmail.com (real-device execution)
Environment: Real VR device; live tour data; validation aligned to the current analog-thumbstick interaction convention
2024 baseline: Issue created 2024-10-14; Unity 2022.3.44f1; Meta XR SDK 68.0.1; Oculus XR 4.2.0
Verdict: PASS

Scope and acceptance alignment

The developer description is preserved separately in the GitHub issue. The task originated during the 2024 Oculus SDK transition, but its acceptance is evaluated using the application's current VR interaction convention: scrolling is performed by analog thumbstick while gaze is on a scrollable panel. The former upper/lower arrow buttons are not present in the current flow and are not treated as an acceptance requirement or defect.

The tester confirmed that all requested real-device checks passed. No device log, screenshot, or video attachment was supplied in this run.

Execution summary

ID Representative scenario Method Result Real-device outcome
SC-01 Open All Tours with a long real-data list Black-box PASS Scrollable list was available.
SC-02 Gaze on All Tours and scroll upward/downward with analog thumbstick Black-box PASS List moved correctly with thumbstick input.
SC-03 Release thumbstick while gaze remains on the list Black-box PASS Scrolling stopped after input release.
SC-04 Scroll at the upper and lower list boundaries Black-box boundary PASS No overflow, jitter, freeze, or crash reported.
SC-05 Move gaze away from the All Tours list, then use thumbstick Gray-box negative PASS Scroll interaction stayed scoped to the scrollable area.
SC-06 Repeat opening/closing the list and scrolling five times Black-box regression PASS No UI corruption or responsiveness failure reported.
SC-07 Scroll a hotspot with a long description Black-box regression PASS Hotspot description scroll worked correctly.
SC-08 Verify runtime errors after scroll interactions White-box runtime evidence PASS (tester confirmation) No app error/crash reported; no log artifact supplied.

Code review

Area 2024 implementation evidence Assessment
Thumbstick input ScrollerThumbstick reads primary and secondary OVRInput.Axis2D thumbsticks while its ScrollRect is hovered. PASS: real-device scroll behavior passed.
Direction and range Scroll value is applied to verticalNormalizedPosition and bounded to 0..1. PASS: direction and boundaries passed.
Gaze scope Pointer enter/exit controls whether a scroll panel accepts thumbstick input. PASS: off-panel negative scenario passed.
Release behavior Zero thumbstick input clears the scrolling state. PASS: scrolling stopped on release.
Regression surface All Tours and long hotspot descriptions both rely on scrollable UI. PASS: both representative surfaces passed.

Test-method coverage

Method Coverage Result
Black-box All Tours analog scroll, stop behavior, boundaries, repeated open/close, long hotspot description PASS
Gray-box Gaze-gated interaction, informed by the thumbstick-scroll implementation PASS
White-box Review of input/range logic plus tester-confirmed runtime outcome PASS; no device log artifact attached
Confusion matrix Predicted scrolling defect versus real-device behavior No defect confirmed

Confusion matrix

Prediction Real-device observation Classification Action
Analog scroll might fail after SDK/UI changes All representative scroll scenarios passed False Positive Do not file a coding bug
Current analog scroll expected to work Direction, stop, scope, boundaries, and regression checks passed True Negative Mark QA passed

Findings

  • No coding bug was confirmed.
  • Absence of the legacy arrow controls is expected current behavior and is not a defect.

QA decision

Issue #40 passes real-device validation against the current analog-thumbstick scrolling behavior while retaining its 2024 SDK-task context.

QA Summary: Issue #41 - Update Vibration Controller

Date: 2026-07-30
Tester: testergothru@gmail.com (real-device execution)
Environment: Real VR device; live tour data
2024 baseline: Issue created 2024-10-14; Unity 2022.3.44f1; Meta XR SDK 68.0.1; Oculus XR 4.2.0
Verdict: PASS

Scope and evidence boundary

The developer description is preserved separately in the GitHub issue. The task is assessed against its 2024 Oculus/Meta SDK context and current real-device user behavior. The tester confirmed that every requested vibration scenario passed. No device log, screenshot, or video attachment was supplied in this run.

Execution summary

ID Representative scenario Method Result Real-device outcome
HB-01 Select an interactable with the right controller Black-box PASS Right controller gave brief vibration.
HB-02 Select an interactable with the left controller Black-box PASS Left controller gave brief vibration.
HB-03 Rapidly select five times with the right controller Black-box stress PASS Each select vibrated; no stuck vibration reported.
HB-04 Rapidly select five times with the left controller Black-box stress PASS Each select vibrated; no stuck vibration reported.
HB-05 Alternate left and right controller selections Gray-box PASS Vibration occurred on the controller making the selection.
HB-06 Select hotspot/other interactable in a real tour Black-box real-data PASS Vibration remained functional with live tour interaction.
HB-07 Wait after an interaction Black-box boundary PASS Vibration stopped automatically.
HB-08 Perform the above interactions during normal app use White-box runtime evidence PASS (tester confirmation) No freeze, crash, or visible app error reported.

Code review

Area 2024 implementation evidence Assessment
SDK availability Meta XR SDK 68.0.1 resolves its Haptics package through com.meta.xr.sdk.all. PASS: package graph contains haptics support.
Controller routing Left and right RayInteractor selection events invoke vibration for LTouch and RTouch respectively. PASS: controller-specific device checks passed.
Vibration lifetime The implementation starts a short coroutine and resets vibration to zero after the configured duration. PASS: stop-after-interaction behavior passed.
Repeated selection Each controller has an independent coroutine reference; an earlier vibration is stopped before a new one begins. PASS: rapid-repeat scenarios passed.
Real-data interaction Haptic feedback is wired to controller selection, including live-tour interactables. PASS: live-tour scenario passed.

Test-method coverage

Method Coverage Result
Black-box Left/right selection, repeats, stop behavior, and live-tour interaction PASS
Gray-box Per-controller event routing, informed by the 2024 implementation PASS
White-box Package/source review plus tester-confirmed runtime outcome PASS; no device log artifact attached
Confusion matrix Predicted haptic-routing/lifetime defects versus real-device behavior No defect confirmed

Confusion matrix

Prediction Real-device observation Classification Action
Vibration might fail or route to the wrong controller after SDK changes Left/right, alternating, and real-tour scenarios passed False Positive Do not file a coding bug
Vibration expected to stop after each interaction It stopped correctly after every validated interaction True Negative Mark QA passed

Findings

  • No coding bug was confirmed.
  • The real-device result takes precedence for user-facing haptic behavior; no implementation change is requested.

QA decision

QA Summary: Issue #42 - Update Gaze Feature

Date: 2026-07-30
Tester: testergothru@gmail.com (manual real-VR execution)
Environment: Real VR application; live tour data
2024 baseline: Issue created 2024-10-14; Unity 2022.3.44f1; Meta XR SDK 68.0.1; Oculus XR 4.2.0
Verdict: PASS

Scope and acceptance alignment

The developer description is preserved separately in the GitHub issue. This validation follows the 2024 gaze behavior: the gaze setting's crossed-pointer icon means Gaze is enabled. The gaze indicator is expected only when the user looks at a supported panorama hotspot or navigation arrow; it is not expected as a permanent menu-center pointer.

The tester confirmed the expected ON/OFF behavior in the real VR app. No device log, screenshot, or video attachment was supplied in this run.

Execution summary

ID Representative scenario Method Result Real-device outcome
GZ-01 Enable Gaze using the crossed-pointer setting icon Black-box PASS Gaze was enabled.
GZ-02 Look at a supported hotspot while Gaze is enabled Black-box PASS Expected gaze interaction behavior occurred.
GZ-03 Look away before target activation completes Black-box negative PASS No unintended interaction was reported.
GZ-04 Use a second supported hotspot after the first interaction Black-box regression PASS Interaction remained usable without duplicate triggering.
GZ-05 Look at a panorama navigation arrow/link Black-box PASS Expected navigation-gaze behavior occurred.
GZ-06 Look at empty/non-supported space Gray-box negative PASS No false activation was reported.
GZ-07 Disable Gaze using the setting icon, then look at a supported target Black-box negative PASS Gaze behavior stopped when disabled.
GZ-08 Repeat enable/disable and supported-target interactions White-box runtime evidence PASS (tester confirmation) No freeze, crash, wrong-target selection, or visible error reported.

Code review

Area 2024 implementation evidence Assessment
Gaze state Settings toggle persists and applies the isGaze state through SetGaze. PASS: ON/OFF real-device behavior passed.
Target gating A forward ray detects supported hotspots and navigation-arrow targets; the indicator is not a permanent menu pointer. PASS: validated against the correct target-only behavior.
Delayed activation Supported targets use a configured delay before automatic action. PASS: expected target interaction passed.
Negative path Gaze is cleared outside supported targets and when the setting is disabled. PASS: no false activation reported.
Hotspot safety The gaze path checks a hotspot action before invoking it. PASS: supported hotspot flow passed.

Test-method coverage

Method Coverage Result
Black-box Toggle behavior, hotspot interaction, navigation-arrow interaction, repeatability PASS
Gray-box Target-only indicator behavior and negative non-target path, informed by raycast routing PASS
White-box Review of 2024 gaze-state/target code plus tester-confirmed real-VR runtime result PASS; no device log artifact attached
Confusion matrix Predicted Gaze state/target-routing defect versus actual device behavior No defect confirmed

Confusion matrix

Prediction Real-device observation Classification Action
Gaze might not activate after Oculus SDK changes Crossed-pointer ON state activated expected hotspot/arrow behavior False Positive Do not file a coding bug
Gaze should remain target-specific and stop when OFF No permanent menu-center indicator expected; disabled state stopped interaction True Negative Mark QA passed

Findings

  • No coding bug was confirmed.
  • The gaze indicator is target-specific. Its absence while looking at normal menu space is expected behavior, not a defect.

QA decision

Issue #42 passes manual real-VR validation for the 2024 Gaze feature behavior.
